text:
maddie: heads up — SLO alert: hosted-infer p99 latency + 5xx spike in euw1, multiple customer escalations coming in. dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/euw1/d/hosted-infer

opsbot: [alert] SLO: hosted-infer.euw1 p99 latency > 1.2s (5m) — rule_id=inf.slo.p99.euw1

sam: seeing +3% 5xx on the gateway metric, spike started ~1769512260. any trace coverage for that window?

luis: running a narrow logs query now for 1769512200-1769512400, focusing on upstream handshake errors. query: ```logs | filter(service=="gateway" and region=="euw1") | json | sort desc```

maria: tracing shows large sampling gap between 1769512250-1769512350 for inbound requests — likely where the p50->p99 stretched. we only have traces for ~10% of requests in that window.

support_jane: Customer ACME reported repeated 502s when calling /v1/generate, they sent one example request id: req_0a9c. Quote: "sudden 502s for last ~5 minutes, nothing changed on our side"

alex: quick repro from inside corp-net: ```curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"redwood-13b","prompt":"hi"}'``` -> HTTP/1.1 502 
response body: `{"error":"upstream_timeout"}`

sam: I see a cluster-level open file descriptor spike on the proxy + long connect times to infer-backend pods. could be connection churn.

luis: digging into kube events: multiple kube-proxy restarts on that node around 1769512245, also kernel dmesg shows "nf_conntrack: table full" warnings. possible conntrack exhaustion.

maddie: interesting — conntrack full would drop new connections and cause transient 5xx. which customers hit it vs probes?

maria: probes were mostly green — but probe paths are small and cached, not representative of real traffic (longer seq lengths). production requests show tail latencies and 5xx.

sam: I can repro locally by hammering the gateway with keepalive disabled; when connections aren't reused we see fd churn and intermittent 502s.

opsbot: deploy-bot: rollout started candidate/gateway@rev-2312 by @ci-user at 1769512300

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: rollout completed for gateway@rev-2312 in euw1 at 1769512380

alex: are we sure this is network conntrack and not the batcher running out of sockets to infer-pool? logs show `accept: resource temporarily unavailable` on gateway.

luis: kernel netstat: high TIME_WAIT count, conntrack table at 100% of configured max. adding more conntrack would buy time but root cause is client-side retry pattern + no keepalive.

sre_lead: mitigation: 1) increase conntrack size on affected nodes (short-term), 2) enable keepalive enforcement in gateway config, 3) rate-limit retries on client-facing LB. who can handle 1 now?

maddie: I can push sysctl conntrack bump and coord with infra to roll node-cta. sam, please prepare a small gateway config hotfix to force keepalive/timeouts and disable aggressive retries in the LB.

sam: on it. patch: ```env.GATEWAY_KEEPALIVE=1; env.CLIENT_RETRY_MAX=2``` will be staged in canary.

support_jane: letting ACME know we're investigating; I'll tell them we suspect transient node network resource exhaustion and we'll follow up with RCA and ETA.

maria: note for RCA: tracing gap likely due to sampling agent overload during conntrack spike — include agent metrics and span drop counts.

alex: also flag for product: some customers hit billing auth errors during the 5xx window — looks like token refreshes queued and failed due to connection drops; could appear as billing/auth break noise.

maddie: summary/action items:
- sam: roll hotfix canary (keepalive + retry cap) — target 10m
- maddie: bump conntrack on impacted nodes and monitor — target 5m
- luis: collect dmesg, conntrack metrics, kube events and upload to incident doc
- maria: compile tracing sampling stats and missed-span counts
- support_jane: customer comms (ACME) update in 15m

last: anyone see follow-ups or objections? :eyes: 

opsbot: [incident] incident created: INC-2026-1769512345 by maddie

maddie: ok starting the sysctl now, tagging infra. will update thread with duration and postmortem link once we have logs.
